followups.q: Who could I partner with for cross-promotion near the top storefront?
followups.answer:
Near 555 Waverly Avenue, start with:

• Fulton Area Business (FAB) Alliance — its district boundary is 48 m away. Ask for introductions to independent shops and opportunities for a joint opening-week promotion. Contact: contactus@faballiance.org or (718) 928-3322.

• Energy Fuel Fulton — juice bar, 162 m away. Propose reciprocal receipts or flyers to introduce customers to your Korean lunch and tea menu.

• Bergen Bagels — 144 m away. Explore neighborhood welcome offers, while checking overlap with your breakfast menu.

• The Bakery On Bergen — 375 m away. Consider a guest-pastry collaboration if it complements rather than duplicates your own pastries.

These are nearby businesses identified in NYC Open Data, not confirmed willing partners. FAB is the best first outreach for broader neighborhood introductions.

followups.q: Why is the top pick better than a storefront in Morningside Heights, where the student share is highest?
followups.answer:
555 Waverly is stronger on the city-records lease score—not necessarily better for your student-focused concept.

Morningside Heights’ college share is 43.7%, at the 99th NYC percentile. That supports your argument, although it doesn’t establish that students will visit a particular storefront.

Its highest-scoring reported vacancy, 11 Hancock Place, compares with Waverly as follows:
• Korean lease-score percentile: 68 versus 89.
• Korean competitors within 400 m: zero at both.
• Korean openings within 800 m since 2024: zero versus one.
• Nearby weekday subway entries: 21,733 versus 7,017—an access proxy, not proven demand.

So Waverly leads on recorded Korean opening-pattern fit; Hancock offers stronger neighborhood student concentration and subway access. The original shortlist doesn’t establish an overall winner. I’d tour both and verify campus walking routes, rent, and build-out costs before choosing.
